newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ISSUES $9.123 MLN DEPOSIT GUARANTEE BONDS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ISSUES $9.123 MLN DEPOSIT GUARANTEE BONDS.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry said on Monday it had issued $9.123 million three-year coupon T-bonds to cover payments to depositors in banks the courts have declared insolvent.
"The bonds were issued to compensate holders of foreign currency deposits in Trade and Savings Bank," a Finance Ministry official told Reuters.

Coupon payments are due semi-annually. Interest on the paper is set at two percentage points over the average six-month London interbank offered rate (LIBOR) for the respective period preceding each coupon payment.
Principal payments are due in three equal annual installments with the first due in May 1998.
The bonds were placed with the state Bulgarian Post Bank (BPB) under a State Deposit Guarantee law approved last year.
So far, BPB has serviced repayment of foreign currency deposits in insolvent banks while the State Savings Bank has repaid lev-denominated deposits.
Trade and Savings Bank was ruled bankrupt by the Sofia City Court on April 10 on the basis of an insolvency claim filed by the central bank in October 1996.

The new issue added to previous three issues of three-year T-bonds worth a total of $79.2 million. They were placed with the BPB last year after the central bank sought insolvency for five local banks.
